solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Understand articles in Greek

indicators.note: the articles are placed in the middle of the abbreviation for Greek

parts.note: A and THE are the indefinite and definite articles

explanation.surface: Someone tries to make sense of the grammar of Greek articles.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather is to infer or come to comprehend, as in 'I gather you were away'.

clue.text: Note doctor breaking a regulation and complain

parts.note: G is a musical note

indicators.note: the doctor piece breaks into the middle of the regulation

parts.note: a rule is a regulation
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine

explanation.surface: A doctor gets a note saying he broke the rules and protests.
explanation.definitionFit: To grumble is to moan or express discontent.

clue.text: Difficult task for brotherhood of high standing

definitions.meaning: a ... read literally as a lofty religious order

explanation.definitionFit: A tall order is a hard request, and literally a tall religious order of brothers.

clue.text: Breaks out, but the rest somehow holds up

indicators.note: holds means contains, so the rearranged letters wrap around the other piece
somehow suggests the letters of rest are reworked in some way

explanation.surface: Trouble flares up, but everyone else somehow keeps going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds up' reads as delays, but 'holds' is the container signal and 'up' the inner piece; 'but the' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcano or a riot that erupts bursts out violently.

clue.text: A fashion editor's heavenly body

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or remake, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the word editor's taken with its S as fodder

explanation.surface: A fashion editor is hailed as a gorgeous celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' reads as part of a job title, but it is a verb telling you to rework the editor's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor planet orbiting the sun is a celestial body, a rock in space.

clue.text: Watch money dribble away

parts.note: to see is to watch
P is penny, a small coin

explanation.surface: Someone sees their savings trickle away.
explanation.definitionFit: To seep is to leak slowly or ooze out.

clue.text: Obtaining one's degree externally

indicators.note: the degree word lies outside, enclosing the other piece

parts.note: extent means degree or measure
one is I, so one's is I'S

explanation.surface: A student earns a degree by external study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obtaining' here means existing or prevailing, as in 'the conditions obtaining', not acquiring.
explanation.definitionFit: Conditions that obtain are in force, real and current.

clue.text: Unusual chore for painters

indicators.note: unusual signals that the word chore appears in an odd arrangement

explanation.definitionFit: This earthy yellow pigment is a colour artists use.

clue.text: Unusually angered and upset

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters of angered set out in an odd way

explanation.surface: Someone is strangely furious and distressed.
explanation.definitionFit: To derange is to disturb or throw into disorder.

clue.text: Dotty pair from Düsseldorf?

parts.note: the two dots over the u in the German city name form a diacritical mark

explanation.definitionFit: The two-dot accent over German vowels, as in the ü of Düsseldorf, is this mark.

clue.text: Explain crack?

definitions.meaning: to make clear the meaning of something obscure
to break a code or puzzle out a cipher

explanation.definitionFit: Decoding handwriting or a code means both interpreting it and breaking it.

clue.text: Instructs, but doesn't allow to fly

definitions.meaning: to ground someone is to teach them the basics
grounding keeps an aircraft or pilot on the ground

explanation.definitionFit: To ground means both to give basic teaching and to forbid a plane from taking off.

clue.text: A lobster is mistaken for fish

indicators.note: being mistaken means the letters are confused into a wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone muddles a lobster with some other fish at the market.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloaters are herrings cured whole by salting and smoking, a kind of fish.

clue.text: Scattered the rest around two quarters

indicators.note: around signals the letters of rest being turned about into a new order

parts.note: W and N are two compass points, west and north

explanation.surface: The remaining items lie spread about the town's districts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' suggests districts of a town; here they are compass points, west and north. 'the' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Strewn is a past participle meaning spread untidily over an area.

clue.text: One who begins a race but doesn't finish it

definitions.text: One who begins a race but doesn't finish it

parts.words: One who begins a race but doesn't finish it
parts.note: sounds like a runner who drops out, but means the official who fires the gun

explanation.definitionFit: The official with the gun sets the field running and plays no further part.

clue.text: Destroys ambitions

explanation.definitionFit: Ends are purposes one strives for, and to end something is to finish or kill it.

clue.text: As a precaution the judge needs to be

definitions.meaning: a phrase meaning to be safe should something happen
a judge should be fair (just) when sitting in a legal case

explanation.definitionFit: Doing something for safety's sake is doing it in readiness, and a fair judge is just in a lawsuit.

clue.text: Lock in the experts, they only pretend to work

indicators.note: the lock goes in the middle of the experts

parts.note: aces are experts
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Lock the specialists in a room; they only fake being busy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they only pretend to work' is a playful definition: these performers' work is pretending.
explanation.definitionFit: Female performers on stage and screen make their living by pretence.

clue.text: No occasion for generosity in the interim?

definitions.meaning: the period in between, as in 'in the interim'

explanation.definitionFit: The intervening period is called this, and read apart it is a stingy occasion.

clue.text: Gives up on French supplies

parts.note: sur is French for on
renders means provides or gives

explanation.surface: A general capitulates over French provisions.
explanation.definitionFit: To surrender is to yield or hand over, which is to give up.

clue.text: Close shaves?

parts.note: narrow escapes, but also the scraping a razor does

explanation.definitionFit: Narrow escapes from danger are scrapes, as a razor scrapes the face.

clue.text: Can make a move

definitions.meaning: to begin moving, as in waking and stirring

explanation.definitionFit: Stir is British slang for jail, and to stir is to move slightly.

clue.text: Pulls out or turns in

definitions.meaning: goes to bed for the night

explanation.definitionFit: To retire is both to withdraw and to go to bed.

clue.text: Music right for one making records?

parts.note: a score is written music

explanation.walkthrough: 'records' suggests discs, but this is the person keeping the tally of points in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A scorer keeps the record of points in a match.

clue.text: Nation embraces popular French dramatist

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a race is a people or nation
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A country takes to its heart a well-loved French playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Racine was a seventeenth-century French tragedian, author of Phèdre.

clue.text: Bill rises after I get in credit — it's about time

indicators.note: after places the bill piece behind the rest
get in means enter, so the letter goes inside credit
rises in a down clue means read upwards, back to front

parts.note: AC is account, a bill

explanation.surface: The bill goes up once I'm in credit; it's high time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about time' looks like an idiom; 'it's ... time' is a link, and the definition is 'about', for an approximate date.
explanation.definitionFit: Circa is Latin for around, used before approximate dates.

clue.text: During exam a head leaves in this

indicators.note: during means within, so one piece sits inside the exam word

parts.note: a test is an exam
each means per head, as in five pounds a head

explanation.surface: A head teacher walks out in the middle of an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb about the head departing; it is tea leaves, stored in this box.
explanation.definitionFit: A large wooden box for shipping tea holds tea leaves.

clue.text: When upset, go on about a monstrous person

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the word over, read backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: When annoyed, a brute goes on and on about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When upset' turns GO into OG; 'on' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairy-tale giant who eats people; figuratively, a cruel or frightening person.

clue.text: Breakfast for bird?

definitions.meaning: oatmeal cooked in water or milk, eaten in the morning
British slang for a prison sentence, from rhyming slang bird-lime, time

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang both 'bird' and this word mean time served in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Porridge is an oat breakfast dish and also British slang for a spell in jail.

clue.text: It enables a writer to eliminate unwanted characters

definitions.text: It enables a writer to eliminate unwanted characters

parts.words: It enables a writer to eliminate unwanted characters
parts.note: sounds like a novelist cutting people from a story, but means a rubbing-out tool for letters

explanation.definitionFit: A rubber tool removes pencil marks, the written letters a writer does not want.

clue.text: Out-of-this-world advertising agents

parts.note: astronauts are out of this world

explanation.definitionFit: Astronauts travel beyond Earth, and salespeople of ad space could punningly share the name.

clue.text: Many pay increases result in disasters

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, hence many
rises are increases in salary

explanation.surface: A lot of wage hikes end in catastrophe for the economy.
explanation.definitionFit: Crises are times of acute danger or trouble, emergencies.
